data.name: Niyathi
data.gender_notes: Niyathi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Niyata', meaning 'fixed, firm, permanent, or true'. Niyathi represents the embodiment of loyalty and dedication to the principles of Dharma. The name Niyathi carries the meaning “Loyal to Dharma” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Niyathi usually hope their child will grow to embody loyal to dharma and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner strength and determination to remain true to one's path in life.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Niyathi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

vedic_reference.note: Niyathi is a Sanskrit name that means 'Established Female'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'niyat', which means 'settled' or 'established'. This name is not directly mentioned in any Vedic text or mythology.

historical_references.reference: Niyathi, also known as Niyati, is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata as the name of a goddess associated with truth and righteousness. She was invoked by Arjuna during the Kurukshetra war to help him maintain truthfulness and righteousness in his actions.

Another reference to Niyathi can be found in the Puranas, where she is described as the goddess of morality and virtue, and is sometimes identified with the goddess Dharma. She is believed to reside in the heart of all beings, ensuring they adhere to the principles of righteous living.
